report.question: add-zone-rules-from-iana cannot be implemented in the factory sandbox as planned: the sandbox only reaches registry.npmjs.org. From this round, data.iana.org returns 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403', and github.com, ftp.iana.org, www.iana.org, jsDelivr and unpkg all fail (curl 000). Local tools are fine: zic, zdump, gpg and tar are installed (Ubuntu 24.04), but /usr/share/zoneinfo is missing. Three tasks need the network. tasks.md 1.1 compiles the newest tzdata archive for the size spike. 3.1 pins the tz coordinator's key through WKD and github.com/eggert/tz. 3.6 runs zone-rules:compile, which downloads https://data.iana.org/time-zones/releases/tzdata<release>.tar.gz and its .asc (design.md D7, spec 'Compiling a release'). Almost everything after 3.6 reads the committed packages/client/zone-rules/release.json: virtual:zone-rules in the tests, the abbreviation table (7.1), the zdump check (10.1, M2), the asset budget (6.3, M5) and the E2E. A checkbox task may not depend on a handoff item (.gnomish/stages/specify/handoff.md). The other spec defects are already fixed in commit 7b2e91d. How should the IANA archive reach the implement stage?
options: A human commits tzdata<release>.tar.gz, its .asc and the tz coordinator's public key (with the verified fingerprint) under packages/client/zone-rules/source/ on main first. The compiler reads these local files and verifies the signature offline, and the change is re-specified for that
The implement sandbox will be given access to data.iana.org (and WKD/github.com for the key), so the change proceeds as written

Split the change: this one ships the reader, the future rule, the wrapper, the compiler and the zdump check, tested on fixtures that the system zic compiles from hand-written zone source. A follow-up change, run where IANA is reachable, commits the real release and switches the app to it
